Part 2&3 人物 PEOPLE AI 补全经历

Describe a child who loves drawing/painting

描述一个喜欢画画的小孩

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe a child who loves drawing/painting

  • Who he/she is (他/她是谁)
  • How/when you knew him/her (你什么时候/怎么认识他/她)
  • How often he/she draws/paints (他/她多久画一次)
  • And explain why you think he/she loves drawing/painting (并解释为什么你觉得他/她喜欢画画)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe a child who loves drawing/painting

I'd like to talk about my little cousin, who is about six years old now. She's my aunt's daughter, and she absolutely loves drawing, which is why she came to mind right away. Actually, I've known her since she was born, but I really noticed her passion for drawing about two years ago, when she started kindergarten. Her mum told me she would come home and spend ages at the table with her crayons, drawing characters from the cartoons she watches. As for how often she draws, it's basically every day. Whenever I visit my aunt's place, she's usually sitting there with a pile of paper, and she'll happily show me her latest pictures. She mostly draws anime characters and cartoon versions of our family, which I find really cute. The reason I think she genuinely loves drawing is that she gets completely absorbed in it. When she's drawing, she goes quiet and focused, which is rare for a kid her age, since she's normally full of energy and running around. She doesn't draw because anyone tells her to, she just does it for fun, and she's always proud to show off the result. Looking back, I think that kind of pure enjoyment is what real passion looks like, and I hope she keeps it as she grows up.

讲的是六岁的表妹，阿姨的女儿，特别喜欢画画。两年前上幼儿园时注意到她的热情，每天回家都用蜡笔画动画片里的角色。她几乎天天画，去阿姨家总能看到她趴桌上画，画动画角色和家人的卡通形象。觉得她真爱画画是因为她画的时候特别专注安静，没人逼她，纯粹为了开心，画完还骄傲地展示。

Q2What is the right age for a child to learn drawing?

I'd say there isn't really a fixed right age, but around four or five seems natural. At that age, children have enough control over their hands to hold a crayon properly, and they're curious about everything. I don't think formal classes are necessary either, since giving them paper and pencils at home is enough to get started. The key is that they enjoy it, rather than learning it as a serious skill.

没有固定年龄，四五岁比较自然，那时手部控制力够、好奇心强；不需要正式培训班，家里给纸笔就行，关键是孩子享受画画本身。

Q3Why do most children draw more often than adults do?

I think the main reason is that children draw purely for fun, without worrying about whether the result looks good. They just put whatever is in their imagination onto paper, and they're happy with it. Adults, on the other hand, tend to judge their own work, comparing it with professional art, so they feel discouraged and stop. In other words, children draw because they enjoy the process, while adults are too concerned with the outcome.

孩子画画纯粹为了好玩，不担心画得好不好看，想到什么画什么就很满足；大人反而会评判自己的作品、跟专业画作比较，容易受挫放弃。孩子享受过程，大人太在意结果。

Q4Why do some people visit galleries or museums instead of viewing artworks online?

I think it's because seeing art in person is a completely different experience. In a gallery, you can see the actual size, the texture of the paint and the details that photos simply can't capture. There's also the atmosphere, the quiet rooms and the lighting, which help you focus on the work. Online, you tend to scroll past images quickly, whereas in a museum you naturally slow down and really look.

现场看画是完全不同的体验：能看到真实尺寸、颜料质感和照片拍不出的细节；还有安静的房间和灯光营造的氛围，让人专注。网上看画容易快速划过，在博物馆里会自然慢下来认真看。

Q5Do you think galleries and museums should be free of charge?

I'd say yes, at least for the main collections. Museums play an educational role, so charging a high entrance fee would stop many people, especially students and low-income families, from visiting. That said, I think it's reasonable for special exhibitions to charge a fee, since they cost a lot to organise. On balance, keeping the core collections free encourages more people to engage with art and culture.

基本同意免费，至少常设展应该免费，因为博物馆有教育功能，高票价会挡住学生和低收入家庭；但特展收费合理，因为布展成本高。总体常设展免费能鼓励更多人接触艺术文化。

Q6How do artworks inspire people?

Artworks can inspire people in several ways. For one thing, they show us different perspectives, helping us see familiar things in a new light. They also express emotions that are hard to put into words, which can make people feel understood. And for some, a powerful piece of art sparks creativity, encouraging them to try making something themselves. So inspiration often comes from the way art opens up new ways of thinking.

艺术作品从几个方面启发人：展示不同视角让人重新看待熟悉的事物；表达难以言说的情感让人感到被理解；强大的作品还能激发创造力，鼓励人自己动手创作。

Q7What are the differences between reading a book and visiting a museum?

I think the main difference is that reading is a private, imaginative experience, while visiting a museum is physical and social. When you read, you build the scenes in your own mind, and you can go at your own pace. In a museum, you see real objects with your own eyes, which is more direct, and you often go with other people, discussing what you see. So books engage your imagination, whereas museums engage your senses.

主要区别：读书是私人的、靠想象力的体验，场景在脑中构建、节奏自己掌握；逛博物馆是实体的、社交的体验，亲眼看到真实物品更直接，还常和别人一起边看边讨论。书激发想象，博物馆调动感官。
